notes: At five years the founding stock saturates K's provisioning multiplier, subsistence never goes short, and the knowledge metrics do not touch the economy. A gate that moved far here would have meant the change reached further than intended.

The universe these numbers describe is still degenerate, and the changes folded into this file moved which ways rather than removing them. Two items leave the list: library depth is no longer pinned near two distinct nodes, because scribing survives now that parchment and bread are different things; and universities the god funds now actually get finished, so completedUniversities is no longer identically one. What remains degenerate: the god is still passive in the two fast gates, so 400 of the 432 runs measure the simulation's own evolution and not play; ascension eligibility still opens by passive accumulation, so the ascension rate remains a statement about a clock; the scribable list is still cost-ordered, so the same cheap nodes are copied repeatedly; and several observation channels still saturate. Read every figure here as a vital sign of a build, not as a description of the finished game.
rationale: Merge of origin/main into w29/city-and-supply-chain (PR #42), and the baselines are regenerated because both parents are invalid against this tree. Provenance first: this tree loads contentRevision 2c67315ae04ee6c74dfa204474af4eb6 and the superseded baseline was recorded at d37624e36be00f59cf21b87ff6eba144, so its numbers describe a different build and a delta against them is a category error rather than a regression. Two movements meet here and only one of them is in the delta below. W17's value-sensitive acquirer (contracts.md 2.11) is the movement the superseded baseline describes -- and this branch already contained it, which is why autonomy-weight.json merged add/add byte-identically and why referenceNodesKnown at five years reads 29.46 here against main's 29.44 and the pre-acquirer 22.115. What this branch carries that main lacks is the whole of the delta, and it is three landed changes rather than one: W6's five ascension constants, W8's raid-engagement constants, and this branch's own economy wire -- the single materials scalar became three kinds (food, stone, vellum), and knowledge reached the economy for the first time, every baseline in this repository before it having been recorded against a build in which resourceYieldBonuses was a hardcoded empty array and advanceConstruction had no caller outside its own tests, so both economy primitives were unreachable by any path. The merge's own finding, worth recording because it is what a reader will want to check: this tree reproduces the branch's committed figures exactly, metric for metric, in all three gates, so main's 104 commits since the merge base moved nothing any of these sweeps can see and there is no acquirer-by-economy interaction to report. These numbers are a measurement of what this build did on this date and NOT a balance claim: release-plan.md forbids one before 0.5.0, every magnitude the change introduced is marked untuned, and nothing here has been tuned against a target. Measured against the superseded baseline in this 200-run 600-tick gate: every one of the nine metrics is inside tolerance. The largest are referenceGrimoires 85.760 -> 83.700 (-1.27 SE) and referenceKnowledgeInstances 406.010 -> 403.320 (-0.92 SE); referencePeakPopulation is identical at 216. Five world years is too short for the economy wire to show, which is the expected result and the same one the note below records.
